title: Stripe webhook ingestion: verified, idempotent, replay-safe
goal: Ingest Stripe webhooks safely: verify the signature on the raw body, persist each event once, process asynchronously and idempotently in any order, and apply resulting plan changes to entitlements.
scope_in: POST /internal/stripe/webhook (not part of the public contract) with raw-body access, signature verification (Stripe-Signature, 300 s tolerance) and a 2xx only after the event is durably stored.
stripe_event table unique on Stripe event id, with status received|processing|processed|failed|ignored and attempts; duplicate events return 200 without reprocessing.
BullMQ job `stripe.event.process` handling customer.subscription.created|updated|deleted, checkout.session.completed, invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed and ignoring others.
Out-of-order safety: on processing, re-fetch the current subscription from Stripe and apply it through B070 upsertFromStripe (stale guard) and B069 applySubscriptionState.

Emit domain events for outgoing webhooks (billing.subscription.updated, billing.invoice.paid, billing.invoice.payment_failed) via an outbox table, and publish a billing_issue notification request on payment failure through NotifyPort.
Replay tooling: an internal function replayEvent(eventId) that reprocesses a stored event.
scope_out: Delivering outgoing webhooks to customers: B081. Notification delivery: B063.
Dunning/grace state machine rules: B078 (this lane records past_due_since only).
Seat sync and invoices listing: B073, B077.
Public contract: Stripe webhooks are explicitly internal.
build_against: Stripe CLI-style signed fixtures generated in tests with the test webhook secret, StripeGateway fake (B070) returning scripted subscription objects, in-memory BullMQ, fake NotifyPort and EntitlementService.
interfaces: WebhookIngest.handle(rawBody: Buffer, sigHeader: string, now: Date): Promise<{status:'stored'|'duplicate'}>

Tables stripe_event(event_id pk, type, created_at_stripe, payload jsonb, status, attempts, last_error, received_at, processed_at), billing_outbox(id, type, workspace_id, payload, created_at, published_at)
Env: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (supports two values for rotation)
acceptance: A body with a wrong signature, a timestamp older than 300 s, or a modified body returns 400 and stores nothing; a valid one returns 200 in < 200 ms (median) after one DB insert.
Delivering the same event id 5 times yields one stripe_event row, one processing run and 200 for each delivery.

Events arriving out of order (subscription.updated with created=T2 before created=T1) end with the subscription state equal to what Stripe's current object says, and entitlements rev increments once per real change.

invoice.payment_failed sets past_due_since once (second failure does not move it), calls NotifyPort billing_issue exactly once per invoice id, and enqueues a billing.invoice.payment_failed outbox row.
customer.subscription.deleted moves the workspace to status canceled/none per mapping and applies entitlements through B069; subscription.updated with seat/plan change updates plan and seats.
A handler failure retries 8 times with exponential backoff and jitter, then marks the event failed and moves it to the DLQ; replayEvent on it reprocesses it successfully after a fix.
Unknown event types are stored with status ignored and return 200; an event for an unknown customer is marked failed with reason `unknown_customer` without crashing.
With two webhook secrets configured, signatures from either verify (rotation test).
No log line or stored column contains card data, the signature header or the webhook secret.
tests: webhook.signature.test.ts: valid, tampered, stale, rotated secret
webhook.ordering.test.ts: out-of-order and stale events (property test)
guardrails: MUST verify the signature against the exact raw bytes before parsing JSON; MUST use Stripe's constant-time verification.
MUST NOT return 2xx before the event row is committed; MUST return 2xx quickly and do work in the job.
MUST NOT trust event payload ordering; always reconcile against the current Stripe object.
MUST exempt this route from user auth but NOT from size limits (max body 1 MiB) and request logging redaction.
MUST NOT change entitlements except through B069 applySubscriptionState.
Handlers MUST be idempotent: replaying any event any number of times yields the same final state.
failure_modes: DB down at ingest -> 500 so Stripe retries; nothing is acknowledged that is not stored.
Stripe API down during processing -> job retries with backoff; events remain `received`/`processing`; alert if oldest unprocessed > 10 min.
Entitlement service error -> event marked failed for retry, subscription row already updated is safe because upsert is idempotent.
notes: No contract implemented (internal), per CT-API-BILLING: 'Stripe webhooks are not part of this contract'. The path /internal/stripe/webhook must be excluded from public docs and protected only by signature; WAF allow-list by Stripe IPs is a B097 option.
